title: Show a derived device-credential lifecycle audit detail

claims.statement: Claude Code (claude-code) is the source-producing agent for CHG-0064 under human principal @rodrigoteamx, on the 2026-08-24 directive to build the next frontier node after CHG-0063 ('dale al merge y a lo que sigue'). This does not authorize automatic merge of CHG-0064.
claims.evidence: AGENTS.md, profile.json actors and the 2026-08-24 user directive.

claims.statement: Before CHG-0064 the Integrations list showed label, scopes, generation and status, but not the credential's provenance or activity timestamps — even though issuedBy, issuedAt and updatedAt were already on the wire in the DeviceCredential list projection.
claims.evidence: studio/src/views/IntegrationsView.vue prior list row and the DeviceCredential = Omit<StoredDeviceCredential, 'sealedSecret'> projection returned by the list route.

claims.statement: The change is UI-only: each credential row shows a lifecycle audit detail derived from its own metadata — issued by and at, last activity (updatedAt) with generation, and revoked-at or expires-at — reading fields already returned by the list route. No server or protocol change.

Governed discovery reordered the work: the audit truth is derivable from the credential's own fields rather than a parallel persisted event log, so the slice derives a lifecycle summary from existing state — avoiding a second source of truth that could drift — instead of building an event store.
claims.evidence: Governed-discovery reorder check on 2026-08-24; the credential record already carries issuedBy, issuedAt, updatedAt, generation and revokedAt.

claims.statement: Showing a per-credential lifecycle detail (issuer, issue time, last-activity time, generation, revocation or expiry) derived from the list metadata, and asserting it renders the issuer and reflects revocation, proves the derived audit view. server/tests/e2e/studioIntegrations.test.ts is the falsification mechanism.
claims.evidence: server/tests/e2e/studioIntegrations.test.ts asserts the audit detail shows 'Issued by' and 'generation 1' at issue and 'Revoked' after revoke.

claims.statement: The derived detail is a lifecycle summary, not a per-event audit log: generation conflates rotations and the revocation, a single updatedAt loses per-rotation timestamps, and issuedBy records only the issuer, not who performed each later change. Per-event 'who did what when' is not provided.
claims.evidence: protocol/src/device-credential.ts: generation is bumped by both rotate and revoke; the record keeps one updatedAt and one issuedBy.

claims.statement: The summary's limits are evidence that derivation is insufficient for a true per-event audit; whether to persist a per-event credential lifecycle log is a genuine decision (a new persisted source of truth) that stays deferred as an ADR candidate, not promoted on this thin evidence.
claims.evidence: Governed-close overstatement check on 2026-08-24; the derived detail cannot reconstruct per-rotation timestamps or per-event actors.

claims.statement: Human review accepted CHG-0064: each device credential shows a lifecycle audit detail derived from its own metadata (issuer, issue and last-activity time, generation, revocation or expiry) on the Studio Integrations surface, reflecting state changes, proving the derived audit view. It is a lifecycle summary, not a per-event log; the persisted per-event credential lifecycle log stays deferred as an ADR candidate.
claims.evidence: studio/src/views/IntegrationsView.vue, server/tests/e2e/studioIntegrations.test.ts, the passing full server suite under npm run check, the CHG-0064 pull-request Constitution run (8 jobs green), and human acceptance on 2026-08-24.

claims.statement: A persisted per-event credential lifecycle log (issued, rotated and revoked events with per-event timestamp and actor) remains deferred to a successor and would be an architectural decision in its own right.
claims.evidence: No credential event store exists; the derived detail is read from current state only.

claims.statement: No server or protocol code changes; the change is the Studio view and browser-test assertions on the existing issue, rotate and revoke lifecycle.
claims.evidence: git diff of the CHG-0064 branch: studio/src/views/IntegrationsView.vue and server/tests/e2e/studioIntegrations.test.ts only.

successCriteria.statement: Each credential shows a lifecycle audit detail derived from its metadata (issuer, issue time, last-activity time, generation, and revocation or expiry).
successCriteria.verification: The browser test asserts the audit detail renders the issuer ('Issued by') and the generation for the issued credential.

successCriteria.statement: The derived detail reflects state changes.
successCriteria.verification: After the credential is revoked, the audit detail records the revocation ('Revoked').

successCriteria.statement: No existing behavior regresses and the surface type-checks.
successCriteria.verification: The full server suite passes and the Studio type-check passes.

definitionOfDone.statement: CHG-0064 records the derived audit slice — the fields surfaced, its lifecycle-summary limit, and the deferred per-event log — before implementation.
definitionOfDone.evidence: Schema-valid record and deterministic governance compilation.

definitionOfDone.statement: IntegrationsView renders a per-credential lifecycle audit detail from existing metadata; a browser test proves it renders provenance and reflects revocation.
The browser test and the full server suite pass.
Governance, licensing, lint, type-check, focused and full tests, build, dependency audit and diff checks pass before handoff.
definitionOfDone.evidence: npm run governance:check, npm run check, npm run build, npm audit (0 vulnerabilities), ESLint, type-check and git diff --check; the accept commit is verified by its own pull-request Constitution run before merge.
